reads.monthly_note:
April was the recovery month. Three Charter Township paychecks (vs the usual two) pushed income to $9,342 — the highest in the dataset. With no lump debt payments and disciplined discretionary spending, the household ran a $2,079 surplus.

Liquid balance rebuilt from $3,151 to $5,230, fully recovering March's deficit with room to spare. The $500 investment transfer to Schwab continued on schedule. Debt service dropped to $295 (just the regular Lake Trust and Chase payments) after March's $1,803 lump event.

This is the month that demonstrates what the household economy looks like when income is elevated and no one-off events hit: healthy surplus, balance rebuilding, investment pipeline flowing. The question is whether this is the norm or the exception — the trendline needs more months to tell.
